LESSON: READING 13.4.1 ORAL LITERATURE: PRAISE SONGS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.4: Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs, part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we sing? 2. What are the qualities of a good singer?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 13.4.1 Oral Literature: Praise Songs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Self-efficacy is strengthened as the learner shares ideas on the relationship between the singer and the person being praised

in a praise song.

 Creativity and imagination are enhanced as the learner gains new perspectives on how to do things as they collaborate to

present praise songs to the class and share experiences.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner values human dignity while collaborating with peers to perform praise songs.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Life skills – The skill of living with others is inculcated as the learner identifies and performs praise songs.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates performance skills to other learning areas such as Creative Arts.
